title: Operating a stream: consumer lag, backpressure, replay and reprocessing

videos.script: Friday, six in the evening. The stock program has run for three weeks, and nobody has looked at it. {{quiet}} Tonight the tills send twenty sales a second, and the program handles ten. {{rates}} Nothing fails. There is no error and no alarm. The website just shows the stock from a minute ago, then ten minutes, then an hour. {{stale}} That gap has a name, consumer lag. It is the first number anybody running a stream learns to watch. {{lag}} In this lesson you make a consumer fall behind on purpose, and you measure how far. In messages, and in seconds. {{measure}} Then you break it three more ways. A consumer too slow between two polls is thrown out of its group. One bad message stops a whole partition. And a bug fixed on Wednesday means reading Monday again. {{break}} Each one has a tool, and a rule for when to use it. {{tools}} By the end, you will know which numbers deserve an alarm at three in the morning, and which can wait for the morning. {{alarm}}
